ground_truth.description: focusOnBounds() duplicates the camera positioning logic from fitToView() (line 189) and flyToEntity() (line 220). The center/size calculation, FOV distance computation, and camera+controls update are identical across all three functions. The existing functions should be refactored to call focusOnBounds() instead of duplicating the same 12 lines of camera math.

focusOnEntities() is nearly identical to fitToView() — both compute a bounding box from meshes and position the camera. The only difference is fitToView uses all meshes while focusOnEntities uses a subset. fitToView could be implemented as focusOnEntities([...getMeshes().keys()]).

focusOnBounds() applies a padding multiplier (default 1.2) to maxDim before computing camera distance, while the existing fitToView() and flyToEntity() do not. This means focusOnBounds-based views will have 20% more whitespace around the target than direct calls, creating inconsistent zoom behavior.

task.title: Add bounding-box and multi-entity camera focus to the viewport selection manager
task.description: The measurement tool needs to frame the geometry it has just measured, but the selection manager in `gui/src/viewport/selection.ts` only exposes whole-scene and single-entity framing. Add two functions to the selection-manager factory and surface them on `SelectionContext`: `focusOnBounds(bounds: Box3, padding?: number)`, which centres the perspective camera on an arbitrary world-space box along the current view direction, and `focusOnEntities(entityPaths: string[])`, which builds the combined box of the named meshes from `getMeshes()` and frames it. Both must also move the orbit-controls target to the box centre when `controls` is supplied, so the next drag orbits around what was framed. An empty box — no bounds, or no path in the list resolving to a live mesh — is a no-op and must leave the camera where it is.
task.test_strategy: Unit-test both helpers against a stub `PerspectiveCamera` and `controls`: framing a known box puts the camera on the current view axis at the expected distance, leaves `camera.lookAt` on the box centre, and copies that centre into `controls.target`. Cover the no-op paths — an empty `Box3`, and an entity-path list whose paths are absent from `getMeshes()` — by asserting the camera position is unchanged. Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` in `gui/`.
